Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
revision_notes: Original sources (CEIC, TheGlobalEconomy) verified and cross-checked against World Bank/ITU data via FRED. Mobile cellular subscriptions stood at 125.6 per 100 people in 2024 (down from 129.2 in 2023 and a 2022 peak of 163.4), and have exceeded 100 per 100 people continuously since the early 2010s. These figures measure SIM/subscription penetration rather than the "unique subscriber" metric the guidelines specify (GSMA Intelligence); no direct GSMA unique-subscriber figure for Seychelles was located. Given Seychelles' small, affluent, highly-connected population, unique subscriber penetration exceeding 70% is highly plausible, but this is an inference rather than a direct match to the specified metric, so the confirmed top-of-scale score is flagged for human review.
revised_comments: Mobile cellular subscriptions in Seychelles stood at around 126 per 100 people in 2024 according to World Bank/ITU data, having exceeded 100% since the early 2010s and peaked near 165% in 2019. This reflects SIM/connection penetration rather than a unique-subscriber count, but Seychelles' small, affluent and highly connected population makes unique mobile subscriber penetration above 70% highly likely.

Definition: Percentage of national population with access to electricity (grid or off-grid). This is the primary indicator of energy infrastructure availability for ICT. Based on World Bank/IEA Tracking SDG7 data, national statistical offices, or Afrobarometer surveys.
revision_notes: World Bank SDG7 Electrification Dataset confirms Seychelles' electricity access rate at 100.0% for 2023, consistent with the 100% figure originally cited for 2022. Score of 5 (90%+) reconfirmed with the more recent data point.
revised_comments: Access to electricity in Seychelles is universal, with the World Bank's SDG7 Electrification Dataset recording 100% of the population with access as of 2023.

Definition: Whether the country has established policies, regulations, and programmes supporting off-grid and distributed energy solutions (mini-grids, solar home systems). These are critical for extending ICT infrastructure to unserved areas beyond the central grid.
Comments: No policy needed; universal grid access ([RES4Africa](https://res4africa.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/RegulatoryReviewofElectricityMarketinSeychelles.pdf))
revision_notes: The cited RES4Africa review (2021) found no dedicated off-grid/distributed-generation regulation and recommended one be developed. Since then Seychelles has enacted the Electricity Act 2023 (Act 13 of 2023) and the Electricity (Distributed Generation System) Regulations 2024 (S.I. 84 of 2024), which establish net metering, net billing, feed-in-tariff and auto-generation provisions, administered by the Public Utilities Corporation (PUC) and the new Utilities Regulatory Commission. PUC's own site describes grid-tied rooftop PV as already "gaining increasing popularity" under a net-tariff arrangement, alongside utility-scale projects such as the Ile de Romainville 5MWp solar farm (2021) and Port Victoria wind farm (2013). As Seychelles already has universal grid access, dedicated off-grid mini-grid needs are minimal, but the distributed-generation regulatory framework is active with demonstrated deployment, so the score is revised upward from 1 (No policy framework) to 3 (Active policy with some deployment).
revised_comments: Seychelles has an active regulatory framework for distributed energy generation under the Electricity Act 2023 and the Electricity (Distributed Generation System) Regulations 2024, which establish net metering, net billing and feed-in-tariff arrangements administered by the Public Utilities Corporation and the Utilities Regulatory Commission. Grid-tied rooftop solar PV is increasingly popular among small and medium consumers, complemented by utility-scale renewable projects including the Ile de Romainville 5MWp solar farm and the Port Victoria wind farm. As the country already has universal grid access, dedicated off-grid mini-grid programmes are not a priority, but distributed-generation policy is active with demonstrated deployment.

Definition: Percentage of total electricity generation from renewable sources (hydro, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass). Indicates energy sustainability and potential for distributed power solutions relevant to ICT infrastructure in off-grid areas.
revision_notes: World Bank/IEA data confirms a 4.51% renewable generation share in 2021, consistent with the original <10% score. A more recent World Bank press release (June 2025) states renewable energy accounted for "just 5%" of Seychelles' total electricity generation in 2023, with a national target of 15% by 2030. Score of 1 (<10%) reconfirmed with the fresher figure.
revised_comments: Renewable energy accounted for around 5% of Seychelles' total electricity generation in 2023, according to the World Bank, with the energy system still reliant on imported fossil fuels for over 95% of generation. The government has set a target of 15% renewables by 2030 under its National Energy Policy 2010-2030 and the newly launched Renewable Energy Acceleration Program (REAP).

Definition: The gap between urban and rural electricity access rates. A smaller gap indicates more equitable energy distribution, critical for ensuring ICT infrastructure can serve the whole population, not just cities.
revision_notes: World Bank data confirms urban electricity access at 100% in 2023. Rural access data (most recently reported at 100% as of 2020 in the World Bank SE4ALL series) combined with the national rate of 100% in 2023 indicates rural access has also reached 100%, giving a gap of 0 percentage points. Score of 5 (Gap <10pp) reconfirmed.
revised_comments: Both urban and rural electricity access rates in Seychelles stand at 100% according to the latest World Bank data (2023), leaving no measurable gap between urban and rural electrification.

Definition: The number and activity level of technology hubs, incubators, accelerators, and co-working spaces focused on technology and innovation. These provide physical infrastructure and support for tech entrepreneurship and skills development.
revision_notes: The originally cited 2019 AfriLabs-Briter Bridges directory listed no Seychelles hubs, but this source is now nine years old. UNCTAD's 2024 Science, Technology and Innovation Policy Review of Seychelles confirms the operation of the government-backed Business and Technology Incubator (BTI), established in 2019 under the Division of Science, Technology and Innovation (DSTI). Additional institutional hubs have since emerged, including the University of Seychelles' UniSey Centre for Innovation (established 2025) and a Seychelles Tech Park referenced by the Department of Information, Communications Technology. A promotional blog (Nucamp, April 2026) also lists several private coworking/incubator spaces (Coboat, Blend Seychelles, Oasis Seychelles) but these were not independently corroborated against authoritative sources and are not relied upon for the score. Based on the three confirmed institutional hubs, the score moves from 1 (None identified) to 3 (3-9 hubs with regular activity). Given the significant jump from the original score and the mixed quality of supporting sources, this is flagged for human review.
revised_comments: Seychelles has a small but growing network of technology and innovation hubs, anchored by the government-backed Business and Technology Incubator operating under the Division of Science, Technology and Innovation since 2019, the University of Seychelles' UniSey Centre for Innovation (established 2025), and a Seychelles Tech Park referenced by the Department of Information, Communications Technology. Additional private coworking and incubator spaces have also emerged, though several are recent and not yet independently verified.
